# Human-Centered Design That Makes Government More Accessible


October 16, 2026


by Jamie Clark


##


More than 1 million Marylanders visit the Office of the Governor’s website each year as a primary means of interacting with state government — but over time, usability testing and website analytics revealed that some content was difficult for users to find quickly.


To make it easier for Marylanders to find information, access needed services, and interact with state government online, the Office of the Governor launched a redesigned website. The result is a cleaner, more intuitive experience built around what residents actually need: one that streamlines access to important information and helps site visitors take action more efficiently.


## Boosting Accessibility


Maryland has a long history of prioritizing accessibility across its digital ecosystem, and the Governor’s Office website redesign built on that work.


All redesign priorities align with the state’s accessibility guidelines (and reflect[NASCIO’s 2026 State CIO Top 10 Priorities](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/resource-downloads/state-cio-2026-priorities-playbook) , in which accessibility ranks number six), which include descriptive alt-text for images, captions and transcripts for audio and video, sufficient color contrast between the text and background, clear, readable fonts, and flexible layouts that adapt to different screen sizes and orientations.


To ensure accessibility of all content and bring documents and PDFs up to the same standard as the pages linking to them, Maryland worked with Tyler Technologies, the state’s longtime partner, to conduct a full content review, going through the site page by page to decide what to keep, update, archive, or remove. New plain-language content was written wherever it made the biggest difference, such as in consistent page titles, introductions, and descriptions to better orient users to the content on each page.


##### Prioritize Accessibility to Improve Resident Experience


Explore how[Tyler is helping states improve the usability of software](https://www.tylertech.com/resident-experience-access-and-accessibility) , reduce barriers to participation in online services, and create a seamless digital experience for residents.


## Improving Navigability


While information on the site was previously organized around how Maryland government is structured, the new design prioritizes user needs, with simpler navigation, improved search functionality, and clearer content structure. From user feedback and site analytics, user personas and journey maps were built to guide decisions about navigation, layout, and language.


One example can be found on the new site’s home page, which now includes a “Featured Services” section organized around what residents are trying to do. The section includes entries like “Join Boards & Commissions” and “Find Grants & Funding,” each with a short, plain-language description that links to the coordinating office behind it. In addition, a separate “Offices, Councils & Workgroups” listing in the site’s top menu offers a page where each coordinating office has its own plain-language summary, so users can easily understand what each office does and where to find needed services.


The updated site structure also adjusts how news and updates from the Governor’s Office itself are organized. Previously, nearly everything the Governor’s Office did publicly lived under “News,” including bill signings, proclamations, and other official actions. The redesigned site introduces “Official Actions” as its own top-level section, separating these formal actions from press releases and making them easier to find. Additionally, press releases now cross-link to related services and resources so a single release can guide someone toward the broader information they are searching for, with deeper tagging improvements still underway behind the scenes to strengthen those connections over time.


## Prioritizing the Resident Experience


Using site visitor feedback and analytics to fuel redesign priorities, the updates made to the website for Maryland’s Office of the Governor are rooted in human-centered design. Rather than organizing information around how state government is structured, redesign efforts started from what residents actually need, how they actually speak about government services, and how they behave when navigating the site. The updates also align with the[Maryland Digital Playbook](https://digital.maryland.gov/) and the state’s commitment to making government information usable by everyone — not just those familiar with government systems.


“The redesign of the Governor’s website reflects what is possible when government, technology partners, and local expertise come together around a shared goal: delivering a better experience for Maryland residents,” said Shannon Pierce, general manager of Tyler in Maryland. “I’m proud of the Maryland-based Tyler team that helped support this effort alongside the State of Maryland and our valued vendor partners. Together, we created a more accessible, intuitive, and resident-centered digital experience that makes it easier for Marylanders to find information, access services, and engage with their government.”
